decision or result: The GPUI+CEF shell (crates/vsesvit-gpui) targets Windows as well as Linux. On Windows it is a build-time choice: the vsesvit crate gets a cargo feature that swaps vsesvit-winui for vsesvit-gpui; WinUI stays the default until the GPUI shell reaches parity. A runtime switch would ship WebView2 and CEF (~200 MB) in one package for no user gain.

CEF glue, state and GPUI views are shared; only native embedding (host window, focus, overlays, screenshots, top-level-at-point) and the message pump differ per OS, behind one platform module with linux/x11 and windows backends.

decision or result: As spike-ext-win proposed decision 3, not section 1.3's toplevel: a hidden WS_CHILD (ignores WM_CLOSE) of the oldest browser window with an attached surface. A surface's detach moves it to the next browser window before its own window goes. With no browser window it waits in a hidden WS_POPUP anchor, a toplevel, so an Alloy browser created then could still activate the anchor: boot should attach the first window's surface before creating the maintenance browser.

A plain GDI child of a GPUI window never shows: GPUI's window is WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP, so there is no surface for it to paint into (PrintWindow read black where it was). Chromium's children render through DirectX and show. The probe's stand-in pages are layered children, which DWM composes from their own surface; the content host has no background brush because it could not show either.
evidence: native_probe capture: page [0,0,0] with a GDI child, [32,128,192] with a layered one
